equivalents.note: The Tibetan transcribes the rāga name as sha ba ri, which points to Śabarī or Śavarī rather than Śīvarī, and the same string could spell Śabarī or a Śabaripa elsewhere in the text, so it is not marked clear.
The Tibetan has cha shas, 'part', as if reading Sanskrit aṃśa for ām̐su, 'fibre', the same word its comment uses for Munidatta's avayava.
The Tibetan reads the carding as examining (brtags, 'examined'), the sense Munidatta gives it in m3, instead of rendering the image.
In place of cotton the Tibetan has tshad mas, 'by valid cognition' (or 'by measure'), as if reading tulā as 'balance, measure'; its comment transcribes the cited word as tu la (m2).
The verse line has lhag ma med, 'nothing remains', for ṇirabara sesu as a whole, while the comment (m2) has cha shas med pa, 'partless', for Munidatta's niravayava.
The Tibetan has 'bab lam, 'path of flowing (or descent)', apparently taking bahala (Munidatta's vahala) from vah-, 'to flow', and its comment cites the line as 'bab (m4).
The line has skra rtse'i cha, 'a hair-tip's portion', and the comment (m4) keeps the hair in both of Munidatta's readings (skra'i rtse mo, skra'i rtse kha), with no trace of his 'fool' (bāla, ajña).
The Tibetan has bya ba byed pa, 'act and agent' (what is done and the doer), and denies them as a pair (zung dag yod ma yin) for the Bengali's kāja na kāraṇa.
The Tibetan puts it in the instrumental, 'through self-awareness Śānti speaks', making it the means of his speaking rather than, as the Bengali can also be read, what he speaks of.
The Tibetan joins the triad to the three worlds with dang ('jig rten gsum dang lus ngag yid), listing the two side by side where Munidatta's Sanskrit sets trailokya and kāyavākcitta in apposition.
Here the Tibetan has rang bzhin gyis nyes pa nyid, 'being faulty by nature', not the rang bzhin gyi skyon it has for the compound in song 5 (cp.05.m2).
The comment transcribes the cited word as tu la instead of repeating the verse line's tshad ma.

The Tibetan splits bhāvopalambhābhāvena into 'apprehending that thing and the absence of thing' (dngos po de la dmigs pa dang dngos po med pa la) instead of 'since there is no apprehension of things'.
The same rnam pa gnyis stands in the verse line (4a) for the song's dui māra, so the Tibetan line already agrees with Munidatta's gloss.
Munidatta's mārgavara is mchog gi lam, and the same lam serves for the song's road in 4a ('bab lam).
